summary: Develop practical ISA-based audit skills in risk, evidence, sampling, estimates, analytics, and reporting. Review the 5-day course outline.
lede: Financial statement auditing training helps audit seniors, controllers, internal auditors, and reporting managers assess risks of material misstatement. Participants practise mapping risks to assertions, evaluating controls and evidence, planning sampling and analytical procedures, testing estimates and disclosures, and documenting findings and reporting decisions; spreadsheet and AI-assisted anomaly checks are introduced as review aids.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, prepare, review, supervise, or communicate financial statement audit work. It suits intermediate practitioners who have exposure to accounting records or audit files and need a more consistent method for risk, evidence, documentation, and reporting decisions.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of financial statements, basic accounting principles, and exposure to audit or financial reporting processes. No programming is required. Spreadsheet experience is useful for the practical analytics exercises. Advanced analytics and AI-assisted review are taught at operational application level, while ISA reporting requirements are applied through guided case work rather than implementation of an entire audit methodology.
